utterances.text: Can you tell us what time of the year it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Summer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now tell us at least approximately what summer month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: July, I believe, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the time of the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Daytime. I don't know. It could have been around between noon and late afternoon. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did your duty last, your shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Well, I can't say it was guard duty, because I wasn't there as a guard. Prisoners were brought to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your task was --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Well, only to watch them, not to let them escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A while ago, you said "they were brought to us"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "us"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: My group of -- the group of men who were stationed at that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what group of men is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: My platoon that was called the "Blue Platoon." We called it that ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that platoon was part of the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If we show you the same photograph again, will you be able to pinpoint the place where the prisoners worked and where you were at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, please. I'm sorry, once again the same photograph, 14.5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please show where the prisoners were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Somewhere here behind this building, somewhere behind this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, but when you say "this building," you have to say it for the record. Does that mean that they were behind Aleksic's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: They also worked in the park, in the park which is here, which was between Rado Polje [phoen] -- that is, the Rado Polje River is behind that park and the Catholic church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please put "2" next to the prisoners behind Aleksic's house and the number "3" at a place where they also worked and where you stood guard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, will you please put it on the ELMO so we can all see it? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell us, this area that you marked, whose area of responsibility was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: The 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one thing I forgot. Where were you then? You said you stood guard, you watched the prisoners. Where were you, physically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Physically, I was watching those working in the park or -- right, yes, that's right, that's right, digging trenches next to the park. There was a fence and there were trees, and they were to remove that and to dig there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point at the place where you were? Is it part of the same positions where you said the prisoners worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, thank you, we do not need the photograph anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion - and I cannot really call it because that is what you said - when you stood guard or didn't stand guard, and you will tell us then what you were doing, were you armed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapon did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: An automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said from midday until late afternoon, you were there and never moved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: No, of course I moved. I didn't stay in one place, but I was there. That was my duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I didn't mean that you didn't walk or whatever. I asked: You didn't leave that area and move to some other place from which you couldn't see the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: No, I didn't, or maybe I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you accept that duty? No, let me rephrase. Were those prisoners Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you accept this duty, since you are a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: I had no choice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: At that moment, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you could move freely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: No, I couldn't. I was free within the city, within the boundaries of the city. I couldn't leave the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you also had permits to move outside the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: No. I was issued that one only later by Vina Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who signed this permit to leave Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned an event in which you took part, and you said that from the hospital you brought some persons, whether they were patients --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: No, no. They were obviously prisoners from Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whose area of responsibility was the area of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. The 4th Battalion, I guess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said -- no. How many prisoners did you say there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. About ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Well, daytime. I wouldn't know the hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's say a month and try to associate it with guarding the prisoners that you marked on the photograph, and you said that it was guarding prisoners, or whatever we call it, that it was in July. Now, did this thing happen in July too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: You know what? Again, I must be quite honest with you. I really am not sure whether it was June, July, August, early September. I really have no idea when that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then a logical question comes to me. Why are we then talking to you here today if you cannot give us any specific answer, because this is such a long interval, especially in wartime. Every day things take place, I mean, which are -- momentous things happen and they simply stick in one's memory, and still you cannot answer the simplest question. And just a while ago, you said these prisoners happened in July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Well, you know what? Perhaps it is imprinted in one's mind if one goes through a diary of these events. But if one was a participant in the events, I think it is only natural for a man not to be quite sure, to have certain doubts about what happened when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that apply to everything that you told us today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: No, because then I would have said that I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember your statement that you gave to the investigators of The Hague OTP on the 4th of October, '99?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said then that it happened in July 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: I suppose I did, yes, but I said then "July or August."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you didn't. You said it was July '93, but you couldn't give the exact date.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Possibly, and that is why I'm making this correction now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then is what you said two years ago correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Not necessarily. That is why I'm making this reservation. Something that I'm not sure about, the time that I'm not sure about, I cannot really claim that that was so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know why this is important to us, because you said that that evening you saw something else in Vinko Martinovic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Well, let's go back to prisoners. You said that they put on uniforms. What uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were given some rifles. What did those rifles look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: Well, they looked like real rifles to me. I wasn't aware that they were imitation rifles. That is something that I learnt later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, another witness, Witness Q, testified before the Tribunal, and he described them as ordinary dummy, wooden and not painted rifles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: From the distance that I saw them, they looked like ordinary rifles to me and, to be even more specific, like American rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Q testified yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You've asked your next question --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your microphone, Your Honour. Microphone for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: -- is saying that the second question was asked before we had a chance to read what the reply was, and your voices were talking over. In fairness to this witness, I don't think there's any evidence that we're talking about the same incident to connect the witness yesterday's description with this. I don't think that we are necessarily talking about the same incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you have taken the words from my mouth. That is something that I am out to prove, and you've resolved a lot of problems for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I apologise if I interrupted your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, not at all, not at all. You were following my line of cross-examination, and you have an excellent grasp of what is going on. But we can come back to that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had a permit and you could leave Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they issued for specific periods of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: I could write the dates in, because I was given blank forms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you issued those forms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: A day or two before I left Mostar, and I filled them in at home. I used my own typewriter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only two minutes, I think, Your Honours. Do we have just one -- there is time for one more question, but I cannot finish today. And these are really very important questions and precisely along the same line of questioning or thinking that Judge Clark mentioned a while ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the date that you put in, in that form, that you typed into that form, to leave Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS S
utterances.text: It was September.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I believe this would be a convenient time to make -- to adjourn, and I would then like to go on with my cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for intervening at this hour, but there are some important scheduling matters. I'm sorry to take the witness's time, but perhaps it's more efficient. As the Court knows, we are taking, from our perspective, at least, an important witness out of turn tomorrow. We had expected to call this witness and had planned to call this witness next week, but we were asked, for various reasons I won't go into at the moment, to accelerate this witness. I'm afraid it's likely that this next witness will take the better part of the remainder of the week, and in fact it raises again and I've been asked to raise with the Chamber again - it may be impossible - but whether we may even go into Friday afternoon. However, my question at the moment is: I just wonder if Mr. Seric can give us any indication of how much longer. I'm not trying to rush him, interfere with his cross-examination in any way, but I just wonder if there is any time estimate, because frankly then we may be faced with a situation -- I'm sorry for talking so fast. We may be faced with a situation where we have to then -- well, we may have to start this other witness. And it would be highly unfortunate, I think, to keep this Witness S here then over the weekend for possibly 15 or 20 minutes on Monday. It would be highly unfortunate. So if we could have a little more information, and perhaps both from Mr. Seric, and from the Chamber, in terms of its thinking, we could try to make our plans accordingly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. What's the initial response from Seric? I understand that it's difficult to prejudge the time you're going to use in the cross-examination, but I hope you could do your best to give some thought on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely so, Your Honour. I do not think we shall go beyond that time. I'm not trying to speak diplomatic lingo in order to get out of the scrape.
